title: Ensemble hub: hub.yaml
description: A hub, in ~/.config/ensemble/hub/hub.yaml, run by `ensemble-hub serve`. Its core is its accounts, their roles and what each may do, the port it listens on (`http`) and the LLM backends it uses (`llm`); everything else reaches it through a connector, each always on and each written in `connectors`: the REST API, MCP, the runners' link, knowledge, tasks and sources. A connector may hold adapters the admin picks, in a map that may be empty. Nothing has a default value: every setting is written, except what may be left out because leaving it out means 'not used' (`llm.runners`, `connectors.knowledge.embed`, and a backend's `api_key_env`).

owner.description: The hub's name, such as the organization or the person who runs it.

http.description: The port every connector over HTTP is served on.

listen.description: The address and port to listen on: the REST API at /api/v1/, MCP at /mcp, and the runners' link at /link and /relay. Put a TLS reverse proxy such as Caddy in front for the internet, or listen on a LAN or VPN address.

accounts.description: How people join and sign in, and what each role may do. Users and their tokens are kept in database.db beside this file, not here: `ensemble-hub user add NAME --role R`.

registration.description: How people join. `type` decides which other settings there are.

roles.description: The hub's roles, named as you like, each a list of what its users may do.

connectors.description: Everything that reaches the hub. Each is always on, and each is written.

rest.description: The REST API at /api/v1/ on the hub's port, for scripts and a web UI. No settings: `{}`.

mcp.description: MCP over HTTP at /mcp on the hub's port, for client agents, signed in with an account's token as the API key: share, recall and tasks. No settings: `{}`.

runners.description: The runners' link, WebSockets at /link and /relay on the hub's port: the tasks runners run, and the backends they share. No settings: `{}`.

knowledge.description: The knowledge vault, and how shares become notes.

tasks.description: The tasks the hub keeps, and the trackers whose issues become tasks.

sources.description: Knowledge brought in from outside, such as a mailbox or a chat.

adapters.description: The sources the hub reads, by name. No source adapter is built yet: `{}`.

hours.description: How long a login (POST /api/v1/login) lasts before its session token stops working.

failures.description: Failed logins for one name before it is refused for a while.

minutes.description: How long a name is refused after too many failed logins.

type.description: approval: anyone who reaches the hub may sign up (POST /api/v1/register) and gets a token at once; it works once an admin approves the sign-up and gives a role.

max_pending.description: Most sign-ups waiting for approval at once; more are refused until an admin handles some.

type.description: closed: nobody signs up; an admin adds users.

permission.description: share: keep knowledge in the organization vault. recall: read its notes. tasks: receive the tasks the hub's inbox finds assigned to you. admin: manage users, approve sign-ups, give roles, revoke tokens. compute: have your tasks worked on by other people's runners that work for the hub, with the agents they lend, and use their models. host: connect a runner that works for the hub, for those whose role has compute.

trackers.description: The trackers whose issues, with the label, go to the runners of the accounts they are assigned to, with their progress, questions and results written back. The key is the tracker's name: letters, digits, '-', '_' or '.'. One for now; `{}` for no inbox.

additionalProperties.description: Where the issues are kept. `type` decides which other settings there are.

type.description: local_markdown: a folder of `<id>.md` issues, each with title, assignee, labels, project and status in its front matter. People write them; Ensemble changes only `status` and appends comments.

dir.description: The folder, relative to the hub's directory or absolute. Often a git repository a team shares.

label.description: The signal: an issue with this label is for the helper teams of the person it is assigned to. A second label `<label>:<team>/<agent>` gives it to that agent; without one it goes to the backlog.

poll_seconds.description: Seconds between two looks at the tracker.

vault.description: The vault's directory, a git repository, relative to the hub's directory or absolute. `ensemble-hub init` makes it.

try.description: The models that turn shares into notes, in order. Each share uses the first whose backend answers and serves it; with one model, it is simply used. The model gets no tools: text in, text out.

when_none.description: What happens when none of the models in `try` can be used. fail: the share goes to review/, saying what each backend answered. wait: the share waits and is tried again later.

max_chars.description: Most characters one recall returns, all notes together.

embed.description: An embedding model: each note's vector when it is written, so the distiller and recall find notes by what they mean as well as by their words. Left out: by their words alone.

backend.description: One of the backends of `llm`, OpenAI-compatible (of type openai-compatible-api, or reached through the hub): it serves /embeddings.

model.description: The embedding model, as the backend names it, such as nomic-embed-text.

min_similarity.description: How alike, by cosine similarity, a note must be to the query to be found by its meaning alone. Depends on the model; 0.5 is a start.

llm.description: The LLM backends the hub uses, such as for distilling knowledge. A name is unique across both groups, and is all that `knowledge` names.

runners.description: Backends runners offer (`shares` in their runner.yaml), which the hub calls through their links; it never learns their address or key. `ensemble-hub runner backends` lists what runners offer now. Left out: none.

backends.description: The key is the backend's name: letters, digits, '-', '_' or '.'. `{}` when there are none.
The key is the backend's name here: letters, digits, '-', '_' or '.'.

relayed.description: A backend a runner offers, reached through the hub: OpenAI-compatible, as a runner offers no other kind.

runner.description: The runner that offers it, as the hub knows it: <owner>/<name>, such as ana/gpu-box.

backend.description: Its name in that runner's llm.direct.

llm_backend.description: How the model is reached. `type` decides which other settings there are.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key, sent as x-api-key. Keys are never written in this file.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.

type.description: openai-compatible-api: any /chat/completions endpoint (llama-server, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, a hosted API).

base_url.description: Where the endpoint is, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key. Keys are never written in this file. Leave it out when the endpoint wants none.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.

backend.description: The name of a backend of `llm`.

model.description: The model id the endpoint serves, as its /models lists it.
